title: Arithmetic series
goal: I can find the sum of an arithmetic series.
teach: The sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic series is Sₙ = n2[2a + (n − 1)d], or Sₙ = n2(a + l) when you know the last term l. To find how many terms give a sum, set Sₙ equal to it and solve the quadratic in n.
tvis:
3 + 7 + 11 + … + 79
n3 + 4(n − 1) = 79, n = 20
Sₙ = n2(a + l)10(3 + 79) = 820
watch: Find n first. It is the number of terms, not the last term.

qs.steps:
1. Formula (arithmetic series): Sₙ = n2[2a + (n − 1)d]
2. a = 10, d = −2, n = 20
3. S₂₀ = 202[2(10) + 19(−2)] = 10(20 − 38)
4. = 10 × (−18) = −180

2. a = 1, d = 1, n = 100
3. S₁₀₀ = 1002[2(1) + 99(1)] = 50 × 101
4. = 5 050
